head: a0d7c6e36c378bbb6c826002039aef486bbe0383
title: Collatz: Lean smooth-tower descent at unbounded exponents
body:
## Why this change

The least numerical tripling source can leave the range where smaller-value goodness is known. This pass attacks that escape by minimizing the positive base left after powers of two and three, so an ordinary merger can decrease that base even at arbitrarily large absolute height.

**Collatz remains open.** The new proposition `FrontierMerger` is an explicit universal closing target, not an established theorem.

## Positive results

- Lean constructs a least positive base supporting a bad power of three and the first bad exponent at that base. It proves that the base is odd, prime to three and good; every smaller positive base is good at every 2,3-smooth multiple, and all earlier powers at the same base are good.
- Four physical exit comparisons and a same-base nine-clock return exclude stated cases. The comparisons permit arbitrarily high excursions. For example, 111 reaches 566, which meets 1701 = 7·3^5 at 638; base 7 is smaller than 37.
- At **every fixed exponent r ≥ 2**, a written prime-power construction gives an infinite progression of short-run sources, all 113 modulo 512, that physically merge with a strictly smaller base at the same exponent. Lean proves the general merger and its first-tower contradiction. These cases evade the preceding high-exit and 85-modulo-512 exclusions.
- Lean proves universal convergence iff `FrontierMerger`. Producing its merger for every surviving source is still missing. The case w = 1 and the unbounded exponent remain included.

## Direct tests of closing arguments

An ordinary crossing family refutes unconditional hitting-time and odd-count comparisons. An exact affine-path invariant tests every eligible power on one smaller smooth ray. Rational cycle controls show why ordered mantissas do not imply numerator coprimality and why least-source color cutoffs alone need not force a smaller inverse shadow at any depth. These controls are explicitly separated from ordinary integer cycles and the specific basin of 1.

The five earlier minimum-source modules and their 46 public theorem audits are unchanged. This pass adds five Lean modules with 34 public theorem audits. Two independent mathematical reviews pin the positive core and prefix arguments. No custom axiom, `sorry`, `admit`, or `native_decide` is used.

## Actual validation

- Complete remote science checkout: `ae87464f6fadd2f3db77686c9883ad463198293f`, 756 tracked files.
- Ten project modules rebuilt into an empty object directory with Lean 4.34.1, warnings as errors and automatic implicit arguments disabled.
- All **80** public theorem audits passed; combined transitive axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.
- Eight Python programs passed in normal and optimized modes with identical output and no disappearing `assert` checks.
- All eleven repository validation commands, including bounded regressions, passed.
- Final reports-only checkout: `a0d7c6e36c378bbb6c826002039aef486bbe0383`, 815 tracked files. All 31 research hashes match the science replay; final repository validation passed.

Written infinite progression, valuation and cycle-order arguments retain their stated evidence level; the kernel checks do not certify universal coverage.
